English: Cooking Hearth
A simple open fire pit surrounded by stones, serving as the heart of early castle food preparation. Provides basic meals for the garrison and improves morale.
Scullery
A humble, roofed lean-to for washing utensils and storing basic foodstuffs. Allows more efficient provisioning for defenders and staff.
Outer Kitchen
A wooden kitchen structure built outside the main hall, improving the ability to prepare and store food in greater quantities during sieges.
Stone Kitchen
A sturdier, fireproof kitchen built of stone, equipped with bread ovens and improved storage, making the castle more self-sufficient in times of crisis.
Buttery
A vaulted storage chamber for ale, wine, and fine foods, improving both the quality and quantity of supplies, and enhancing the lords hospitality.
Smokehouse
A dedicated stone smokehouse for preserving meats and fish, ensuring resilience during long sieges and boosting the morale of defenders.
Pantry Hall
A grand hall lined with shelves and storerooms for grain, cheese, and salted goods, allowing for vast reserves and lavish feasts.
Great Kitchen
An elaborate, multi-chambered kitchen complex employing skilled cooks and servants, capable of provisioning vast armies and hosting dignitaries.
Banquet Kitchen
A prestigious kitchen complex with specialized staff for feasts, tournaments, and visiting nobility, greatly enhancing the grandeur of court life.
Royal Kitchen
A legendary kitchen complex fit for a king, combining the finest architecture with the most skilled staff, hosting legendary feasts and cementing dynastic prestige for generations.
